description.narrative: Introduction Climate change and the accelerating demand for green transition are creating urgent challenges for businesses globally, including in Vietnam, one of the world’s most climate-vulnerable countries. Viet Nam ranks 127/182 on the ND-GAIN Index and 13/180on the Global Climate Risk Index, with climate-related losses exceeding USD 10 billion between 2010–2020 (3.2% of GDP). Without timely mitigation and adaptation measures, the World Bank estimates that climate change could cost the country 12–14.5% of GDP annuallyby 2050, and push up to one million people into extreme poverty by 2030. In Hue and Da Nang, climate impacts are increasingly severe, threatening key economic sectors such as agriculture, forestry, tourism, and community livelihoods. Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), accounting for 98% of all businesses are particularly vulnerable. Women-owned businesses (WBOs) face even greater barriers in accessing technology, finance, and market information, and remain underrepresented in climate-related policy processes. This underscores significant capacity gaps and persistent gender inequalities in local green-transition ecosystems. The Initiative, “Strengthening Green Finance Access for MSMEs, Cooperatives (HTX), and Business Support Organizations (BSOs) to Promote Green Transition, Job Creation, and Women’s Empowerment in Climate-Policy Engagement in Hue and Da Nang” (hereafter “the Initiative”), seeks to address these challenges by enhancing institutional capacity, supporting sustainable business models, and strengthening the role of women in climate-action policymaking. Objectives and Activities The Initiative aims to strengthen MSME/HTX and BSO capacities in green finance, green transition planning, and sustainable business development. Key activities include: (i) baseline assessments and gender-responsive needs analysis; (ii) training programs on green finance and green transition; (iii) one-on-one coaching for 10 BSOs and 10 MSMEs/HTX; (iv) development of gender-disaggregated datasets and sustainable enterprise profiles; (v) green finance matchmaking events; and (vi) a policy forum and Demoday to promote dialogue, policy contribution, and investment linkage. Project Areas and Duration The Initiative will be implemented inHue and Da Nang from Jan 2026 to Mar 2027 (15 months), combining capacity strengthening,demonstration models, ecosystem linkage, and policy advocacy. Target Groups and Beneficiaries The Initiative directly benefits fourgroups: BSOs: 20 organizationswill receive capacity building, with 10 supported in designing green-finance advisory services. MSMEs/HTX (with priority to women-owned or women-led enterprises): 60 will receive foundational training, and at least 20 will receive intensive support to develop green-transition plans. Women’s unions, business associations, and women entrepreneur networks engaged asstrategic partners to mobilize WBO participation. Financial institutions, green investment funds, and strategic partners connected through Demoday and policy dialogues to expand collaboration and investment pipelines. Through these actions, the Initiative contributes to green transition, inclusive economic development, and enhanced climate resilience for vulnerable communities in central Vietnam.

participating-org.narrative: The FTU Innovation and Incubation Space (FIIS), established in 2017 under the Foreign Trade University (FTU), is a comprehensive ecosystem that supports entrepreneurship, innovation, and sustainable business development. FIIS provides incubation, capacity building, and advisory services for MSMEs, cooperatives, business support organizations (BSOs), and social organizations. Guided by the belief that every individual can help make the world better through sustainable and innovative ideas, FIIS has become a recognized leader in enterprise support in Vietnam. The center has strong experience in improving financial access, promoting green and circular practices, supporting innovative start-ups, and fostering job creation. FIIS also works to enhance the participation of women and vulnerable groups through training, mentorship, and targeted support. A major area of focus for FIIS is advancing sustainable business models, particularly the Circular Economy (CE), Social Impact Business (SIB), and Inclusive Business (IB). These approaches enable enterprises to create long-term economic, social, and environmental value. Gender equality and social inclusion are embedded across all FIIS programs, ensuring equitable opportunities for women, youth, ethnic minorities, and underserved communities. By combining academic expertise with practical solutions, FIIS equips entrepreneurs and organizations with the skills, mindset, and networks needed to grow sustainably. Today, FIIS serves as a trusted partner to government agencies, development organizations, and private-sector stakeholders working to strengthen Vietnam’s innovation ecosystem.
